_: How the HUD's street plate is drawn (P3-24). JSON rather than a .tres, which
hard rule 4 permits explicitly, because this file has TWO readers in two
languages: scripts/ui/hud.gd draws from it, and tools/font_coverage.py checks
against it. A .tres would mean writing a second parser in Python for a
dictionary literal, and two parsers of one file drift.
The English line is deliberately NOT set in this font. Hong Kong street name
plates carry a Latin grotesque and a Chinese Kai side by side, so the plate
using Godot's built-in Noto Sans above Free HK Kai is the real thing, not a
_substitutions: Characters the published street names use that `font_zh` does not draw,
mapped to the form it does. Applied WHEN THE PLATE IS DRAWN — roadgraph.json
keeps exactly what the Transport Department published, because Q54's rule is
that sourced data is neither invented nor moved and a street's NAME is the
啓 U+5553 is TD's variant; 啟 U+555F is the same character in the form the
Education Bureau's 《香港小學學習字詞表》 uses, which is what this font was
built from. One street in region: KAI CHIU ROAD / 啓超道.
⚠️ This table is NOT a place to correct names. It maps a glyph to the same
glyph in another encoding. A pair whose two sides are different WORDS is a
data edit wearing a font's clothes.
tools/font_coverage.py refuses any character that is in neither the font nor
this table, so a data refresh or a second city cannot quietly ship a tofu
box. It is run by hand, like the other graders in tools/, and CLAUDE.md
lists it as owed on a font or street-name change.
